note: Feel Lab scenes (R131): small hand-made courses built by the real generator (jj_procgen::lab), so a scene shares its pieces' definitions with generated tracks (P1-FL15b). `jj lab <scene> --out <dir>` writes the map and each run's fixture; the committed copies are maps/lab/<scene>.json and scenarios/lab/<run>.json, re-made with JJ_BLESS=1 cargo test -p jj-procgen --test lab. A run starts a car `spawnBeforeM` before the first set piece's lip (from the route's start on a scene without one) at `speedMps`, or with a `verge` at rest on the road facing off it toward the first verge that rises like that; it drives on the autopilot or holding `throttle`, in its `vehicle` (the Cruz without one); `expect` is its outcome envelope, and a verge run's `riseM` bounds the height it ends at over the road.

canyon-leap.what: P1-FL09: the Olgas reference (art/references/australia/generated/biome-rocks-olgas.png). A rock channel with walls both sides, a kicker the full road width, the pit, the far rim as the landing, domes seen from the far straight before the commitment point; the graded dirt detour round the pit is the safe line and costs time (R129).

runs.what: The leap at design speed: the autopilot takes the car from the far straight's end over the pit and lands it upright on the far rim, with no wreck or recovery, and drives on.

Too slow to clear the gap: a car holding a third of the throttle up the kicker leaves the lip far under the piece's lowest landing speed, falls into the pit and respawns (one wreck), never clipping through to the far rim.

off-road-climb.what: P1-FL12 (R133): the off-road climb. An outback oval whose verges rise off the road into banks and rock walls. The Tradie Ute drives off the road's edge from rest and up a bank (generated verges rise at 40-65 degrees); a steeper face reads as a wall, and the Ute can't drive up it.

runs.what: From rest on the road beside the first bank of 40-50 degrees that rises 6 m or more, the Tradie Ute turns square off the road and holds full throttle: it crosses the shoulder and climbs the bank, ending at least 5 m above the road, on its wheels, with no wreck.
The same bank, the same start, in the Cruz Missile: a road car's nose and road tyres stall it near the foot, under 4 m above the road. The climb is the Ute's.

From rest beside the first face steeper than 62 degrees that rises 4 m or more, the Ute holds full throttle into it: the face is a wall. The Ute ends no more than 6 m above the road and doesn't wreck.
The autopilot drives the Ute a full lap of the scene (771 m) from the route's start, with no wreck or recovery.
